# Method for Simultaneous Transmission of Analog and Digital Information with Energy Across a Galvanic Isolation Barrier

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a method for simultaneously transmitting both analog and digital information, together with energy, between a power transmitter and a galvanically isolated power receiver. This approach enables the efficient combination of data communication and power delivery across an isolation barrier, eliminating the need for separate signal and power transmission pathways.

## Digitization and Encoding of Information

In accordance with the method, the analog information is first digitized. This digitization is accomplished by defining a specific number of possible discrete values as well as the value range within which these values may fall. By establishing both the quantity of permissible values and their corresponding range, the continuous analog signal is converted into a discrete representation suitable for transmission.

The digital information, by contrast, is handled by assigning it a binary digital value. In this manner, both the analog and digital components of the information are prepared for encoding within a unified transmission scheme.

## Definition of Event Counts and Value Sets

The method further establishes a minimum and a maximum number of events to be transmitted, thereby bounding the range of event counts used in the encoding process. In addition, two distinct sets of values are defined, denoted as **n_low** and **n_high**. These value sets are derived from functions of the digitized analog values, ensuring that the analog information is systematically incorporated into the determination of the event counts.

## Encoding of Digital Bit Values Through Event Counts

The number of events transmitted serves as the mechanism for encoding the digital bit values. Specifically, for each bit being transmitted, a binary value of 0 corresponds to the value **n_low**, while a binary value of 1 corresponds to the value **n_high**. Alternatively, this assignment may be reversed, such that a 0 corresponds to **n_high** and a 1 corresponds to **n_low**, depending on the chosen implementation. In this way, the digital information is embedded within the same event-based transmission that carries the digitized analog information.

## Signal Transmission and Corresponding Device

Finally, a signal correlating to the determined number of events is transmitted from the power transmitter to the galvanically isolated power receiver. This unified signal conveys the combined analog and digital information alongside the transferred energy.

Beyond the method itself, the present invention also encompasses a corresponding device configured to carry out the described method. Such a device incorporates the necessary components to perform the digitization, encoding, and transmission steps, thereby enabling the simultaneous transfer of analog information, digital information, and energy across a galvanic isolation barrier.

# Combined Analog, Digital, and Power Transmission Across a Galvanic Isolation Barrier

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to systems and methods for transmitting information across galvanic isolation barriers. More specifically, it concerns a technique for the simultaneous transmission of analog information, digital information, and energy between a power transmitter and a power receiver that are electrically isolated from one another.

## Background and Problem Statement

In many electrical and electronic systems, galvanic isolation is essential to protect sensitive circuitry, prevent ground loops, and ensure the safety of both equipment and users. A galvanic isolation barrier physically separates two electrical domains so that no direct conductive path exists between them, while still permitting the controlled transfer of energy and information across the divide.

A persistent challenge in such systems arises when multiple types of information must be conveyed across this barrier at the same time. Traditionally, transmitting analog values, digital data, and power across an isolation boundary requires separate channels or dedicated components for each function. This approach increases circuit complexity, component count, physical footprint, and overall cost. Consequently, there is a significant need for a compact and efficient solution capable of consolidating these transmission functions into a unified method.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these challenges by providing a method that enables the simultaneous transmission of both analog and digital information, along with energy, across a single galvanic isolation barrier between a power transmitter and a power receiver.

At the core of the invention is a technique that digitizes analog values and encodes information through a defined number of discrete events. These events are bounded by predetermined minimum and maximum thresholds, establishing a range within which meaningful event counts can be interpreted at the receiving side.

## Detailed Operation

The method operates by assigning distinct event counts to represent the two possible states of a digital bit—namely, a logical 0 or a logical 1. In this way, the number of events transmitted across the barrier inherently communicates the digital bit state to the receiver.

Simultaneously, the analog value is embedded within these very same event counts. By carefully defining the relationship between the number of events and the corresponding analog magnitude—while respecting the established minimum and maximum thresholds—the method allows a single stream of events to convey both the digital state and the analog value concurrently. The minimum and maximum thresholds serve to delineate the valid operating range, ensuring that the receiver can reliably distinguish between the encoded digital states while accurately extracting the embedded analog information.

Because the events used to encode this information can be tied to the energy transfer mechanism itself, the same activity that delivers power across the barrier simultaneously carries the combined analog and digital data. This dual-purpose use of the transmission events is central to the efficiency of the invention.

## Advantages of the Invention

By combining analog information, digital information, and energy transmission into a single coordinated method, the invention offers several notable benefits:

- **Efficiency:** The consolidation of multiple transmission functions eliminates the need for separate dedicated channels, streamlining the overall data and power transfer process.
- **Compactness:** The reduction in required components yields a smaller physical footprint, making the solution particularly attractive for space-constrained applications.
- **Reliable Isolation:** The method fully preserves the integrity of the galvanic isolation barrier, maintaining the electrical separation necessary for safety and signal integrity.
- **Versatility:** The approach is well suited to a wide range of applications that require electrical isolation while demanding the transfer of both control data and operating power.

## Conclusion

In summary, the present invention provides a compact and efficient solution for the simultaneous transmission of analog and digital information together with energy across a galvanic isolation barrier. Through the digitization of analog values and the encoding of information via defined event counts bounded by minimum and maximum thresholds, the method achieves combined data and power transmission across isolated systems, meeting the needs of applications where electrical isolation is critical.

# Patent Abstract

## Method for Simultaneous Analog and Digital Information Transmission with Energy Transfer Across a Galvanically Isolated Interface Using Event-Based Encoding

A method and system for the concurrent transmission of analog information, digital information, and electrical energy across a galvanically isolated barrier between a power transmitter and a power receiver. The method employs an event-based encoding scheme in which discrete signaling events—characterized by variations in timing, amplitude, frequency, or phase of an energy transfer carrier—are superimposed onto the power transfer waveform. Digital information is encoded by mapping data symbols to the temporal positions or patterns of said events, while analog information is simultaneously conveyed through continuous modulation of one or more event parameters, such as pulse amplitude or inter-event interval.

The galvanic isolation is maintained by an isolation element, such as a transformer, capacitive coupler, or optical coupler, through which both energy and the encoded information are transferred without a direct conductive path. At the receiver, an event-detection circuit recovers the timing and parameter values of the received events, from which the transmitted digital and analog data streams are demodulated and reconstructed, and from which harvested energy is extracted to power receiver-side circuitry.

By combining energy delivery with event-based multiplexing of heterogeneous data types onto a shared isolated channel, the method eliminates the need for separate isolation channels for power, analog, and digital signaling, thereby reducing component count, cost, and physical footprint while preserving signal integrity and isolation robustness. The invention is applicable to isolated sensor interfaces, industrial control systems, medical instrumentation, and power management circuits requiring safe, efficient, and multiplexed cross-barrier communication.

counterfactuals.output:
# Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides systems and methods for encoding and transmitting data across an isolation barrier during wireless power transfer by defining and detecting event counts within the power transmission signal. The invention enables the simultaneous transfer of electrical power and the communication of both analog and digital data across a galvanically isolated interface without requiring a separate dedicated communication channel.

## Overview

In accordance with one aspect of the invention, data is encoded by controlling the number of discrete events—such as switching cycles, oscillation periods, resonant pulses, or energy transfer bursts—that occur during a defined transmission interval across the isolation barrier. A transmitting circuit on a first side of the barrier modulates the power signal to produce a countable sequence of events, and a receiving circuit on a second side of the barrier detects and counts these events to recover the encoded data. Because the same signal conveys both power and information, the system reduces component count, minimizes physical isolation crossings, and improves overall efficiency and reliability.

## Digital Data Encoding

In certain embodiments, digital data is encoded by mapping symbols to predetermined event counts. For example, a first number of events occurring within a transmission window may represent a binary "0," while a second, different number of events may represent a binary "1." Multi-bit symbols may be represented by a plurality of distinguishable event counts, thereby increasing data throughput. The receiving circuit compares the detected count against one or more threshold values or a lookup table to decode the transmitted digital value.

## Analog Data Encoding

In other embodiments, analog data is encoded by establishing a substantially continuous or proportional relationship between the magnitude of an analog quantity and the event count occurring within a transmission interval. A sensed analog value—such as a voltage, current, temperature, or other measured parameter—is converted into a corresponding number of events, such that the count varies as a function of the analog input. The receiving circuit recovers the analog value by measuring the event count and applying an inverse mapping or scaling function.

## Advantages

The disclosed techniques provide several advantages, including: (1) unified transmission of power and data across a single isolation barrier; (2) support for both analog and digital data using a common encoding framework; (3) robustness against noise, since counting discrete events is inherently tolerant of amplitude variations; (4) reduced system complexity and cost by eliminating separate isolators or communication paths; and (5) scalability of data rate and resolution through selection of the transmission interval and the range of permissible event counts.

These and other features and advantages of the invention will become apparent from the detailed description, drawings, and claims that follow.

*Note: This is a template draft intended as a starting point. Specific claim language, technical parameters, and embodiments should be tailored to your actual invention and reviewed by a qualified patent attorney or agent.*

# Patent Abstract

## Signal Transmission Method for Galvanically Isolated Power Systems

A method for transmitting information between a power transmitter (10) and a galvanically isolated power receiver (12) is disclosed, wherein the transmission combines analog and digital information encoding through event counting techniques. The power transmitter (10) generates a sequence of discrete signal events across a galvanic isolation barrier, wherein the number of events within a defined time interval encodes digital information, while at least one physical characteristic of the individual events—such as amplitude, pulse width, or timing—simultaneously encodes analog information.

The galvanically isolated power receiver (12) comprises an event counter configured to detect and tally the discrete signal events to recover the encoded digital data, and an analog decoder configured to measure the physical characteristic of the received events to recover the encoded analog data. The galvanic isolation barrier maintains electrical separation between the transmitter (10) and receiver (12) while permitting signal transmission via an isolation element, such as a transformer, capacitor, or optical coupler.

By employing event counting to convey digital information concurrently with analog encoding within the same event stream, the method enables efficient bidirectional or unidirectional communication of both control parameters and measured operating values across the isolation barrier without requiring separate dedicated communication channels. The method is particularly suited for isolated power converters, wherein feedback regulation signals, status information, and configuration commands may be transmitted with reduced component count and improved noise immunity.
